__comment: NVisionX Cluster Health Overview (all clusters, per-environment via $datasource). Sourced entirely from kube-state-metrics and node-exporter - both always-on cluster components, not app-specific business metrics - so every panel here should show real data regardless of which services are currently idle/scaled to zero. | 2026-08-28: added a "What's Wrong Right Now" section with always-visible detail tables (crash-looping pods with reason+restarts, Failed-phase pods, not-ready nodes with condition, pending pods with age), and click-through drill-down links from the Nodes Not Ready / Pods Failed / Pods Pending / Restarts KPI tiles to their matching detail table, per manager request for the dashboard to be self-explanatory to non-engineers. The plain-English status banner was tried and then removed per feedback - the KPI strip's own red/green tiles already say what's wrong. | Folded in Infrastructure Overview's Network I/O and Storage Usage panels (the only two panels there not already covered here) and deleted that dashboard as a duplicate. | 2026-09-19: fixed the crash-loop table (601) to also catch terminated-container failures (OOMKilled, Error, etc) - it previously only checked waiting_reason (CrashLoopBackOff-style), completely missing containers that die and get marked Terminated instead. Added a $workload picker (unifies Deployment/StatefulSet/DaemonSet names, scoped by $namespace) and a full pod-detail table (id=701) so picking a namespace shows its workloads, picking a workload narrows every pod-level panel to just that workload's pods, and leaving Workload on All shows everything - per manager request.
description: Complete cluster health at a glance: a KPI strip you can click through to see exactly which pod or node is the problem and why.

panels.title: Pods Crash-Looping / Erroring / Terminated (why + restart count)
panels.description: Every container currently either stuck in a bad waiting state (CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, etc) or that most recently terminated abnormally (OOMKilled, Error, etc), with restart count. Restart count is the best available proxy for "how long" - kube-state-metrics doesn't expose an exact failure-start timestamp; for the precise duration, check `kubectl describe pod` or cluster Events.

panels.title: Pods in Failed Phase
panels.description: Pods Kubernetes has marked Failed outright (distinct from crash-looping — these have stopped retrying, usually a one-shot Job pod that errored with restartPolicy: Never).

panels.title: Nodes Not Ready — Why
panels.description: Any node currently reporting a real problem condition (memory/disk/PID pressure, or network unavailable). If a node is Not Ready but shows nothing here, check kubelet/network connectivity directly — not every NotReady cause has its own condition.

panels.title: Pods Pending — How Long
panels.description: Pods stuck in Pending, with minutes since creation. kube-state-metrics doesn't expose the scheduler's reason (insufficient resources, no matching node, etc.) — for that, check `kubectl describe pod` or cluster Events.

panels.title: All Pods — Full Detail ($namespace / $workload)
panels.description: Every pod matching the Namespace and Workload pickers above, regardless of health - this is the complete inventory, not just the failures. Pick a specific workload (Deployment/StatefulSet/DaemonSet name) to see just its pods with full status; leave Workload on All to see everything in the selected namespace(s).

panels.title: Pods by Phase
panels.description: Live snapshot of every pod's phase across the selected namespace(s).

panels.title: Pod Restarts Over Time
panels.description: Container restarts, 5m windows. Should be flat at zero outside deploys.

panels.title: Top Restarting Pods (last 1h)
panels.description: The pods worth investigating right now.

panels.title: Network I/O
panels.description: Node-level network throughput, from node-exporter. Folded in from the retired Infrastructure Overview dashboard.

panels.title: Storage Usage %
panels.description: Root filesystem usage per node, from node-exporter. Folded in from the retired Infrastructure Overview dashboard.

panels.title: Recent Job Failures
panels.description: Every Job object currently reporting a failed status.

panels.title: Namespace Breakdown
panels.description: One row per namespace: total pods, running, failed, and restarts in the last hour.

title: Cluster Health Overview
